Radar plot comparing groups on several variables

Source: R/plot-radar.R
plot_radar.Rd

Each numeric variable gives one axis (mean or median per group); each categorical variable gives one or several axes (proportion of a level per group). Every value is brought to a 0-100% scale (configurable normalisation) with an optional confidence band. A between-group test per axis (Wilcoxon / Kruskal-Wallis / t / ANOVA / chi-squared / Fisher), with a multiplicity correction, adds stars or p-values to the labels.

Usage

plot_radar(
  data,
  vars,
  group = NULL,
  group_levels = NULL,
  group_labels = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  var_order = NULL,
  reverse = NULL,
  force_quali = NULL,
  quali_levels = NULL,
  quali_expand = TRUE,
  quali_sep = " : ",
  stat = c("mean", "median"),
  ci = TRUE,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  ci_method = c("t", "boot", "se", "sd"),
  n_boot = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  normalize = c("minmax", "quantile", "summary", "zscore", "rank", "none"),
  limits = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  z_range = c(-1, 1),
  quantile_probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  normalize_quali = FALSE,
  clip = TRUE,
  test = c("auto", "wilcox", "kruskal", "t", "anova", "none"),
  test_quali = c("auto", "chisq", "fisher", "none"),
  p_adjust = "BH",
  show_signif = TRUE,
  p_values = NULL,
  test_label = NULL,
  signif_format = c("stars", "p", "both"),
  signif_cutpoints = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1),
  signif_symbols = c("***", "**", "*", ".", "ns"),
  p_digits = 3,
  start_angle = 90,
  clockwise = TRUE,
  inner_radius = 0,
  grid_levels = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
  grid_shape = c("circle", "polygon"),
  grid_colour = "grey82",
  grid_linewidth = 0.4,
  grid_linetype = "solid",
  spoke_colour = "grey70",
  spoke_linewidth = 0.4,
  background_fill = NA,
  show_grid_labels = TRUE,
  grid_label_fmt = NULL,
  grid_label_angle = NULL,
  grid_label_size = 3.3,
  grid_label_colour = "grey55",
  palette = "okabe",
  colours = NULL,
  line_width = 1.1,
  linetypes = NULL,
  point_size = 2.8,
  point_shape = 19,
  show_points = TRUE,
  band_alpha = 0.2,
  fill_alpha = 0,
  show_values = FALSE,
  value_digits = 1,
  value_size = 3,
  label_size = 4.2,
  label_colour = "#2C3E50",
  label_fontface = "bold",
  label_offset = 0.1,
  label_wrap = NULL,
  label_lineheight = 0.9,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  legend_title = NULL,
  legend_position = "bottom",
  legend_nrow = NULL,
  show_legend = NULL,
  base_size = 13,
  base_family = "",
  title_size = NULL,
  caption_size = 9,
  plot_margin = c(10, 20, 10, 20),
  expand_x = 0.65,
  expand_y = 0.2,
  return_data = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Wide data frame, one row per subject.

vars

Variables on the radar (names or tidyselect). Numeric: quantitative axes; factor / character / logical: proportions.

group

Grouping column (NULL: one profile).

group_levels

Order of the groups.

group_labels

Renaming of the groups (named old = new, or unnamed in level order).

labels

Axis labels: named vector (variable name, or "variable:level" for a categorical axis) or unnamed vector of one label per axis.

var_order

Order of the axes (variable names, axis ids or labels), starting at start_angle; axes not listed follow.

reverse

Variables reversed (1 - x), e.g. when "higher = better" for some scales and not others.

force_quali

Numeric variables treated as categorical (e.g. 0/1).

quali_levels

Named list: level(s) shown for each categorical variable, e.g. list(SEX = "Female"). Default: TRUE for a logical, the 2nd level of a binary variable, every level otherwise.

quali_expand

If FALSE, a variable with more than 2 levels and no quali_levels gives a single axis (1st level).

quali_sep

Separator of the "variable : level" labels.

stat

"mean" or "median".

ci

Draw the confidence band.

ci_level

Level of the confidence band.

ci_method

"t" (Student CI), "boot" (percentile bootstrap), "se" (+/- 1 SE) or "sd" (+/- 1 SD). For the median, "t" and "se" switch to "boot". Proportions always use the Wilson CI.

n_boot

Number of bootstrap resamples.

seed

Seed of the bootstrap and simulated Fisher tests (NULL: the current random state is used; with a seed, the random state is restored afterwards).

normalize

"minmax" (individual data), "quantile" (same on the quantile_probs quantiles, robust to extremes), "summary" (min-max of the group summaries), "zscore" (SD units around the mean of reference, 50% = reference mean, edges = z_range SD; recommended when group differences are small compared with the range), "rank" (percentile ranks of the subjects, all groups pooled, then mean per group) or "none" (data assumed in [0, 1]).

limits

Named list of fixed bounds per variable, with priority, e.g. list(MOCA_V0 = c(0, 30)) (advised for bounded clinical scales).

reference

Reference group of normalize = "zscore" (NULL: all subjects).

z_range

Range shown in SD units for "zscore".

quantile_probs

Bounds of normalize = "quantile".

normalize_quali

Normalise the proportions too (FALSE: shown as is, 0-100%).

clip

Clip the normalised values to [0, 1].

test

Quantitative axes: "auto" (Wilcoxon with 2 groups, Kruskal-Wallis otherwise), "wilcox", "kruskal", "t" (Welch t / Welch ANOVA), "anova" or "none".

test_quali

Categorical axes: "auto" (chi-squared, or Fisher with expected counts < 5), "chisq", "fisher" or "none".

p_adjust

Method of stats::p.adjust().

show_signif

Add the significance to the labels.

p_values

P-values computed elsewhere (named by variable or axis id), e.g. paired tests between visits; they replace test and test_quali (p_adjust is applied to them).

test_label

Name of the test of p_values, for the caption.

signif_format

"stars", "p" or "both".

signif_cutpoints, signif_symbols

Cut-points and symbols of the stars (length(signif_symbols) == length(signif_cutpoints) + 1, the last symbol meaning "not significant").

p_digits

Decimals of the p-values shown.

start_angle

Angle of the first axis, in degrees (90 = top).

clockwise

Direction of the axes.

inner_radius

Radius of the central hole (0 to < 1), so that small values are not squashed at the centre.

grid_levels

Levels of the grid circles, on [0, 1].

grid_shape

"circle" or "polygon" (spider web).

grid_colour, grid_linewidth, grid_linetype

Style of the grid.

spoke_colour, spoke_linewidth

Style of the spokes.

background_fill

Fill of the disc (NA: none).

show_grid_labels

Print the grid levels.

grid_label_fmt

Function formatting the grid levels (NULL: automatic, %, SD for "zscore", percentiles for "rank").

grid_label_angle

Angle where the grid levels are printed (default: start_angle).

grid_label_size, grid_label_colour

Style of the grid levels.

palette

Palette of the groups (see pal_levels()); default "okabe".

colours

Explicit colours (named by group or not), with priority.

line_width

Width of the profiles.

linetypes

Line types per group (NULL: solid).

point_size

Size of the points.

point_shape

Shape of the points (one value, or one per group).

show_points

Draw the points.

band_alpha

Transparency of the confidence band.

fill_alpha

Fill of the profile areas (0 = none).

show_values

Print the raw (non-normalised) value at each point.

value_digits, value_size

Format of the values printed.

label_size, label_colour, label_fontface

Style of the axis labels.

label_offset

Distance between the labels and the outer circle.

label_wrap

Width (characters) for wrapping the labels (NULL: no wrapping).

label_lineheight

Line height of multi-line labels.

title, subtitle

Titles.

caption

NULL = automatic caption (tests and CI), FALSE = none, or a text.

legend_title

Title of the legend (default: name of group).

legend_position

"bottom", "right", "top", "left" or "none".

legend_nrow

Number of rows of the legend.

show_legend

NULL = automatic (hidden with a single group).

base_size, base_family

Base font size and family.

title_size, caption_size

Sizes of the title and caption.

plot_margin

Margins c(top, right, bottom, left) in points.

expand_x, expand_y

Space around the radar for the labels.

return_data

TRUE: return list(plot, summary, tests).

Value

A ggplot (the tables are in attr(p, "radar_data")), or a list when return_data = TRUE.

Details

The plot is drawn in Cartesian coordinates (not coord_polar()): profiles are straight-sided polygons and the grid is circular or polygonal.

Examples

plot_radar(cohort_sim, c(AGE, BMI, NFL_V0, IL6_V0, MOCA_V0, UPDRS_V0, SEX),
           group = GROUP, normalize = "zscore", quali_levels = list(SEX = "Female"))
